html:
The Corinthian War was fought from 395 to 387 BCE between Sparta and an alliance of Thebes, Athens, Corinth and Argos, backed by Persian money.

After winning the Peloponnesian War, Sparta made enemies of its former allies, who felt cheated of the rewards, and sent its king Agesilaus to fight the Persians in Asia Minor. The Persian king answered by sending gold to Sparta's enemies in Greece.

  • In 395 BCE Lysander was killed at Haliartus in Boeotia.
  • In 394 BCE Sparta won land battles at Nemea and Coronea, where Xenophon fought on the Spartan side.
  • The same year a Persian fleet led by the Athenian Conon destroyed the Spartan navy at Cnidus. With Persian help Athens rebuilt its Long Walls.
  • In 390 BCE light troops under the Athenian Iphicrates wiped out a unit of Spartan hoplites near Corinth.

When Athens began to look too strong, Persia switched sides. The war ended with the King's Peace of 387 BCE, whose terms were set by the Persian king and enforced by Sparta.
sum: The Corinthian War was fought from 395 to 387 BCE between Sparta and an alliance of Thebes, Athens, Corinth and Argos, backed by Persian money.
